column1: # install-parity-allowlist.tsv - reviewed divergences between the twins (SPEC D-ALLOW).
# Nine TAB-separated fields: id, pairs, scenario, path, kind, host, tracker, match, reason.
# A row covers a divergence only for its pair, scenario, path, kind and host; for kind lines every differing
# line must match the match regex of one covering row. Every row has a tracker: accepted (by design) or a
# follow-up id. A row that covers nothing for one of its pairs on a whole-tier run is stale and fails the run.
# A missing row with a fu- tracker may take ? as match: intermittent, it covers when present and is never stale.
# A lines row needs a regex (never -); a regex led by = is paired: its capture group 1 must be equal on both sides.
# A differing line is judged by the FIRST row in file order whose regex matches it, so a narrow row (a path) stands before a paired row that matches every line.

column9: on a host whose sed is BSD (macOS) sh writes two spaces after Template version: where ps1 writes one (BSD sed reads \s as a literal s; GNU sed strips the space, so the twins agree on Linux and Windows); the match is paired (leading =), so the version value must be the same in both twins and a wrong version on either twin stays visible; the module writes one space like the PowerShell twin (DR-21)

ps1 stamps Synced at with seven fraction digits where sh stamps to the second (N1 rewrites only the second-precision shape; the self pair shows two ps1 runs differ by their stamps); the module takes the bash side

ps1 lays the AAI blocks out in a different order with 4 more blank separator lines; the run shows it as a lines divergence (the files also differ in header text, so the order-only kind never fires, seed kind order corrected to lines); the module takes the bash side

column8: ^# AAI (runtime sidecars \(seeded (from \.aai/system/RUNTIME_IGNORE\.list|by aai-sync\.ps1); per-dev, never commit\)|runtime reports \(ephemeral; not project-owned docs\)|per-dev runtime state \(RFC-0001: never committed\))\r?$
column9: the runtime sidecar block header names RUNTIME_IGNORE.list in sh and aai-sync.ps1 in ps1, and ps1 adds two more block header comments sh does not write; the module takes the bash side
sh leaves hooks/session-start.sh executable, ps1 does not (PowerShell copies carry no mode bits on POSIX); the module takes the bash side

sh stamps the sync-conflicts report name in UTC and ps1 in local time, so on a non-UTC host the ps1 name disagrees with its Generated-at line; the driver pairs the two reports by ordinal (their content is compared) and reports the name disagreement alone, at the path ending #name, which is all this row covers; the module takes the bash side
ps1 stamps the report Generated-at line with seven fraction digits, visible on every host now that reports are paired by ordinal; the module takes the bash side

step 2 of HK-09 is the uninstall, which removes the hooks step 1 installed; the self pair therefore differs by design; the module twin's uninstall step removes what its install step wrote, as the twins do
step 2 of SY-06 syncs the core profile over an extended install, which prunes the extended-only files step 1 wrote; the self pair differs by design
the pin records the profile, which step 2 of SY-06 changes by design
the pruning sync of SY-06 step 2 writes a sync-conflicts report step 1 did not; the self pair differs by design

column8: ^(1\. Inspect each item with \x60?git diff -- <path>\x60? in the target project\.|2\. Ask AI to extract project-specific guidance and place it into project-owned docs \(for example \x60?docs/ai/project-overrides/\x60?\)\.)$
column9: ps1 writes the two next-step lines of the sync-conflicts report without the backticks sh writes around the command and the path; only those two lines, in either spelling, are covered; the module takes the bash side

on Windows the sh twin (Git Bash) records the source path in the POSIX spelling /c/... and the ps1 twin records C:\... for the same directory; only a path under an aai-parity-* scratch directory ending in fx/src or syref (the frozen twins run from the syref copy of the scratch source, the module from fx/src) is covered, in either spelling; the regex cannot compare the two spellings with each other, so the scratch directory itself is not checked for equality between the twins

the sync-conflicts report names the source path in the Git Bash spelling /c/... in sh and C:\... in ps1 on Windows; only a path under an aai-parity-* scratch directory ending in fx/src or syref (the frozen twins run from the syref copy of the scratch source, the module from fx/src) is covered, in either spelling, not equality between the twins

the frozen twins run from the syref copy of the scratch source and the module from the scratch source itself, so the pin records two paths for one tree (a harness placement, the module resolves its source from its own location as the twins do)
the report header names the syref copy for the frozen twins and the scratch source for the module, as the pin does

on Windows ps1 writes AAI_PIN.md through Set-Content, which ends its last line with CRLF and, under Windows PowerShell 5.1, starts the file with a UTF-8 byte order mark; sh writes LF and no mark; the row is paired, so every line it covers must hold the same text on both sides once a trailing CR and a leading mark are ignored; the module takes the bash side

on Windows ps1 writes the sync-conflicts report with CRLF line ends and, under Windows PowerShell 5.1, a UTF-8 byte order mark; sh writes LF and no mark; the row is paired, so every line it covers must hold the same text on both sides once a trailing CR and a leading mark are ignored; the module takes the bash side

on Windows ps1 appends its .gitignore blocks with Add-Content, which ends each value with CRLF where sh writes LF; the row is paired, so every line it covers must hold the same text on both sides once a trailing CR is ignored; the module takes the bash side

on Windows the sh twin's update leaves empty root directories of the target whose names are random wide characters (three or four per run, born in the last seconds of the step, while the doctor field report runs) and the ps1 twin leaves none; the driver reports each at the path <odd-root-name> with its real name in the detail, and this row covers those entries of the update scenario on a Windows host only; the module twin runs the doctor helper on its own Node and is compared with the same bash reference
Git Bash spells the target root /c/...; the native module writes the Windows path, which a native Windows bootstrap should record (DR-9)
the frozen twins vendor themselves and the bash library; the module side vendors its launchers, the module and its libs
the frozen twins vendor their own full text and the module side vendors the two launchers in their place; the launchers carry no sync rule, the module holds them (D-LAUNCH)
the frozen twins vendor the bash gitignore library and the module side vendors the module libs lib/resolve-base.mjs and lib/gitignore-block.mjs; the reference tree holds neither of the two
the older-core fixture holds the pre-.aai legacy layout; the frozen twins delete ai/ and the module keeps it (DR-13, D-LEGACY: the moves deleted names a project may own)
the frozen twins delete the legacy ai/ tree and the module keeps it (DR-13)
the frozen twins delete the legacy scripts/aai-sync.sh and its directory, the module keeps them (DR-13)
the frozen twins delete the legacy scripts/ files and the module keeps them (DR-13)
the frozen twins move the loose docs/ai/PRICING.yaml away and the module keeps it (DR-13)

step 2 of SY-06 prunes the extended-only files; the frozen twins also prune the bash gitignore library they vendored (the current core list names the module library instead), so their Deleted items list one more path and its separating blank line than the module run, which never held it
